page.layout: Running head at top centre with page number 244 at left. Two coin medallions side by side near the top, each with marginal legends (illustrations, legends transcribed below). Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs, with no notes or margins.

main_text.p: [The first word is printed in capitals.] SOLYMANUS Turcarum Rex, ex re feliciter prouisa, cui euentus responderit, nomē tulisse fertur, quod Salomonem Sapientiæ gloria inclytū, immutatis syllabis referat. Itaq; Solymano secus ac patri contigisse constat, qui à contrario sensu Selymus, hoc est mafuetus, autorque pacis, sit vocatus: quo nemo Othomanorū ferocior & bellicosior fuerit. Sed Solymani res gestæ, paternæ famæ nomen æquasse censeri possunt. Recepta namque Syria, interfecto Gazelle qui rebellarat, Belgradū fortiter expugnatū, Rhodus manu capta, Buda bis occupata, Austriacus exercitus in fuga cæsus, Rocādulphi ingentes copiæ ad Budā superatæ, expugnatū Strigoniū, & Alba Regalis præclaræ Hungariæ ciuitates, an. 1543. & paulò ante Hispani in Dalmatia ad Castrum nouū expugnati, classibus eorum, quæ insuperabiles viderentur, ad Leucadem fugatis: hæc, inquā, Solymanum patri, aufu nec imparem, nec gloriæ minus auidū testabuntur. Assyriæ præterea & Mesopotamiæ regna, cum Babylonia vrbe, magnæ Memphi æquada, quæ suo Solymanus adiecit Imperio, captæ à patre Aegypto opponi possunt. Quinetiam Solymanus maioris Armeniæ, Mediæ, Perfidisque fines, vsque ad sinū Persicū, vastauit: Taurim Persarū Regiam, bis cepit: Tamasum Sophim, Hismaëlis filium, refugientem ad mōtes, fugauit. Verum quod ad Solymani mores etiā attinet, fatentur sanè Turcę, eius subditi, eum suprà cæteros Othomannorum principes, qui per ducentos regnarint annos, iustitiæ, sobrietatis, & continentiæ laude clarissimum. Vide Paulum Iouium.
ROSSA omnium Solymani vxorum pulcherrima, præter formā multis etiam virtutibus dotata est: quare apud Solymanum præ cæteris omnibus vxoribus maxima pollet gratia, ab eóque vnicè amatur, ac colitur.

page.notes: The head running title reads "PROMPTV." with a doubtful glyph for P (possibly ligatured or Greek-like), transcribed as printed. The coin legends are read from the illustrations and are uncertain: the left legend and the right legend are partly unreadable, so [?] marks them. Spelling is as printed (e.g. "aufu", "Turcę", "Persicū"). The line break "Belgradū for / titer" has no printed hyphen and is written as "fortiter".
